rule: choosers know pages, never pointers; effectors know pointers and pages and decide nothing; pointer literals enter only at the final lowering, as page-table dereferences (operator, 2026-11-02)

violations.chooser holds pointer: a chooser reads or computes an address, a byte offset, a (buffer, offset) pair or a byte width used as an address unit
violations.chooser picks a map by hand: a chooser fixes a ring, a generation, a slot stride, an invocation index or an in-place landing instead of leaving the address map to the solve
violations.chooser has access: a chooser scope imports, receives or can call a pointer-yielding API without deciding with it yet
violations.effector decides: evaluation code makes a placement, storage or layout choice
violations.effector computes a map: generated or native run-time code evaluates an address map that the final lowering could have specialized into a pointer literal or base + affine offset

P1.problem: hand an operand to the native compiler or recorder
P1.replacement: pass the operand's page map (its lease's virtual pages to physical page indices) and its layout in elements; the final lowering dereferences page-table indices into pointer literals

P2.problem: start a kernel, host or provider argument at a byte other than its layout's first element
P2.replacement: the argument's origin is a coordinate of its layout over the page map; the final lowering emits page_table[page] + affine offset as the literal

P3.problem: meet an API's alignment and capacity, and decide between direct use and a copy
P3.replacement: alignment and capacity are constraints of the page-map solve, in pages and in-page elements; no base address is read

P4.problem: relate producer and consumer selections of different scalar types
P4.replacement: typed layouts composed onto one page map, the dtype carried by the layout; the scalar width multiplies only in the final lowering

P5.problem: decide which values share an allocation and how large it is
P5.replacement: two values alias where their page-map images intersect; an allocation's extent is its page map's domain

P6.problem: operate on the same bytes at another scalar width
P6.replacement: a reinterpretation is another layout over the same page map; no storage handle is rebuilt

P7.problem: give repeated occurrences of a call storage that does not collide, or that reuses pages, across invocations
P7.replacement: an invocation -> (virtual page -> physical page) map solved from the occurrences' liveness; the program names no generation, ring, slot stride or invocation index

P8.problem: update recurrent state each step without a new tensor or a copy
P8.replacement: the step returns new values (a functional collective, a functional cell); the invocation page map decides whether a step's result shares pages with the state it replaces

P9.problem: find the region pages a tensor or an address lies in
P9.replacement: region tensors carry their page map from the lease; nothing maps an address or an MTLBuffer back to pages

P10.problem: give a host, CPU or provider entry its operands
P10.replacement: the entry is declared over page maps and layouts; the final lowering alone writes its pointer literals

P11.problem: name the part of a collective's operand each segment, cut or fragment covers
P11.replacement: segments are layouts over the operand's page map, counted in elements

P12.problem: address a view's elements inside a kernel
P12.replacement: the final lowering specializes the map into pointer literals or base + affine offset from the page table; no mesh_index, mesh_storage_N or division by a layout extent at run time

P13.problem: describe a torch view's position in its allocation
P13.replacement: the view is a layout composed onto its lease's page map; storage_offset() is never read

P14.problem: reach layouts, device facts and native helpers that live beside pointer-yielding calls
P14.replacement: split _stream: choosers import a pointer-free module of layouts, page maps and constants; page_backing, host_page_backing, address, records, page_storage and torch storage handles are reachable from the final lowering only

P15.problem: give each value region storage, and give command constants a place
P15.replacement: leases are taken once from the compiled page map at load; nothing places storage by the order of run-time requests
